No blocking correctness finding. Read the PR body first, reviewed all four
changed files and the whitespace-insensitive production diff, and inspected
the installed SDK read-only. No local builds, tests, dependency installation,
symlinks, runtime reloads or source edits were performed.

Installed SDK contract:
- Used the current self-updated CLI 1.0.114-0 runtime's copilot-sdk files,
  not the stale npm launcher package (0.0.412-2).
- extension.js:20137-20173: joinSession preserves hooks and passes tools'
  definitions through to resumeSessionForExtension.
- extension.js:18146,18172-18173,18255,18349: resume registers tools from
  tools.definitions, hooks from hooks.handlers, serializes the tool definitions,
  and advertises hasHandlers from those nested callbacks.
- extension.js:14154-14177,14863-14866,14980-15010: registerTools installs named
  handlers; registerHooks stores callbacks; dispatch selects
  onUserPromptSubmitted/onAgentStop and supplies invocation.sessionId. Missing
  hooks return undefined. types.d.ts:3178-3190,3688-3693 and
  extension.d.ts:6-9 agree with the new nesting.
- The extension's single tool and both configured hooks are nested correctly
  (.copilot/extensions/pij/extension.mjs:90-176). No registered callback was
  left at the old config level. session.on subscriptions are a different API:
  precedence, final-reply tracking, shutdown and NativeBridge activity/progress
  observers remain unchanged. The SDK still supports wildcard and typed on()
  listeners (extension.js:13728-13750). F207/#247 session.idle handling survives:
  store.mjs:1538 and 2222-2234 still subscribe and publish idle only at the
  intended idle/abort/fusion-completion boundaries, not assistant.turn_end.

Compatibility and proof notes:
- 1.0.114 does NOT adapt the old flat shape. Its tool object spread and nested
  lookups discard the old array's useful definitions and ignore flat hooks.
- Installed 1.0.112-0 instead directly passes config.tools/config.hooks
  (extension.js:17946,17975). The new object is not compatible with that old
  tool-array contract. There is no fallback. The documented CLI >=1.0.113 floor
  makes this explicit; older CLI users must upgrade before adopting this
  extension. Backward compatibility is not claimed or a blocker for this fix.
- The fake now mirrors the relevant real nested lookups, missing-hook result,
  invocation session ID and named pij_send lookup. The existing tool/FYI tests
  plus the new stop-hook test exercise the actual extension with that fake.
- Non-blocking follow-up, consistent with C34: this is still a hand-maintained

Restored boundaries and cost:
- Handler bodies and schemas are unchanged. pij_send checks native session
  identity, then NativeBridge.send validates nonempty strings, destination,
  force/reason/FYI combinations and reply ID. It sends JSON over the existing
  HTTP client, never invokes a shell, and derives sender/caller from immutable
  registration rather than model-supplied from/caller fields
  (store.mjs:2345-2430). No skipPermission/approval override or additional

- FYI additionalContext remains the daemon's exact rendered block
  (store.mjs:2288-2305). It is a numbered FYI section with sender/machine
  attribution, timestamps and indented continuation lines
  (crates/core/src/fyi.rs:130-175,249-264), not newly authored system
  instructions. This is attribution/delimitation, not an injection-proof
  sandbox; body rendering and trust semantics are unchanged.
- No new credential read, loop, poll, timer, subprocess or daemon launch site.
  Restored hook work is one HTTP claim per eligible typed prompt and zero or
  one turn-end HTTP call per eligible fenced final reply, zero process launches,
  scaling with events rather than seats per tick. No live before/after launch
